When the day was over, Billy and Sam went home to sleep.

openings.opening:
Lila and Lisa were busy on the sidewalk. The babysitter was not far away.
Lisa found a big blanket. Lisa used some sticks to make a fort on the sidewalk.
Lisa and Lila played a hopping game over a kite string. The rule was no touching the string. It was Lisa's turn, and Lila looked away.
Lisa could have stepped over the string, but Lisa hopped over it instead. Lisa lost the game.
Lisa kicked a little pebble along the path. It rolled and rolled and stopped by a patch of clover.
openings.rest:
Lisa laid Lisa's stick down and walked off to find a ball. Lila stayed right next to the stick.
Lila picked up Lisa's stick and held it out. "You dropped this," said Lila.
Lila sat down on the grass for a moment. A little breeze came by and made the leaves whisper.
The babysitter sat on a chair. The babysitter told Lila to never blame someone else for something Lila did.
Lisa built a tall tower of blocks that leaned to one side. Lila stood right beside it.
"The tower is very tall," said Lila. Lila helped Lisa steady the blocks.
Just then, a yellow leaf floated down and landed near Lila's shoe. Lila watched it wobble in the wind.
Lila found a small box of seeds. Lila put the seeds into the dirt in the garden.
Lila put Lila's bag of dice down and bent to tie a shoe. Lisa was right next to the dice.
Lisa picked up Lila's dice and handed them to Lila. "Here are your dice," said Lisa.
The sun came out from behind a cloud and warmed Lisa's face. Lisa blinked and looked around the yard.
At the end of the day, Lila and Lisa ate dinner and went to bed.

openings.opening:
Sara and Amy were together at the playground. The teacher sat nearby.
Amy put Amy's bag of dice down and bent to tie a shoe. Sara was right next to the dice.
Sara picked up the bag of dice and handed it to Amy. "You dropped this," said Sara.
Sara noticed an ant carrying a crumb across the step. It went one way, then the other, and then it was gone.
The teacher said, "Do not touch the flowers." Then the teacher walked away to talk to someone else. Sara and Amy stayed by the garden.
Sara looked at the flowers but did not touch them. Sara played with the sand instead.
Just then, a yellow leaf floated down and landed near Sara's shoe. Sara watched it wobble in the wind.
openings.rest:
Sara tried to wind up the kite string and got it in a big knot. Amy stood right beside Sara.
"That is a very big knot," said Amy. Amy helped Sara pull the string.
Then Amy noticed a small brown bird on the fence. The bird hopped twice and flew away over the trees.
Rain fell on the playground. Amy found some big puddles. Amy jumped in the puddles.
The teacher sat with Amy. The teacher said, "Never break other people's things."
Sara put Sara's plate of crackers down and went to wash sandy hands. Amy sat right next to the crackers.
Amy picked up the plate of crackers and held it out. "Here are your crackers," said Amy.
Amy sat down on the grass for a moment. A little breeze came by and made the leaves whisper.
Sara turned too fast and knocked a plate of cookies to the ground. The teacher looked at the mess and asked Sara, "What happened here?"
"I knocked the cookies down," said Sara.
The sun came out from behind a cloud and warmed Sara's face. Sara blinked and looked around the yard.
The day ended with dinner and a story before bed.

openings.opening:
The day began under the big tree, where Leo and Lila liked to play. The teacher was with them.
Lila and Leo played a drawing game with a stick. The rule was one line each. It was Lila's turn, and Leo looked away.
Lila could have drawn two lines, but Lila drew only one and lost.
Then Lila noticed a small brown bird on the fence. The bird hopped twice and flew away over the trees.
Lila held a bright kite. Lila ran under the big tree. The kite flew high in the sky.
openings.rest:
The teacher looked at Lila. "Never leave anyone out on purpose," said the teacher.
Lila dropped the board game, and the pieces went everywhere. The teacher looked at the mess and asked Lila, "What happened here?"
"I dropped the board," said Lila quietly.
Lila looked over at the big oak tree. Its branches swayed gently back and forth, back and forth.
Leo dropped the plate of crackers, and they broke into bits. The teacher looked at the mess and asked Leo, "What happened here?"
"I dropped the crackers," said Leo quietly.
Leo kicked a little pebble along the path. It rolled and rolled and stopped by a patch of clover.
Leo held a pretty flower. The flower belonged to Lila. Lila was busy playing nearby.
Leo held the flower gently and handed it back to Lila.
Leo noticed an ant carrying a crumb across the step. It went one way, then the other, and then it was gone.
Leo and Lila played a rolling game with a toy truck. The rule was one push per turn. It was Leo's turn, and Lila looked away.
Leo could have pushed the truck twice, but Leo pushed it only once.
Just then, a yellow leaf floated down and landed near Leo's shoe. Leo watched it wobble in the wind.
The afternoon ended, and the teacher took Leo and Lila home.

openings.opening:
John and Molly spent the morning at the playground. The librarian was there too.
Molly and John played a stacking game with crackers. The rule was one cracker per turn. It was Molly's turn, and John looked away.
Molly could have taken two crackers, but Molly took only one and lost.
Then Molly stretched both arms up high and yawned. Somewhere nearby, a bell rang once and stopped.
John reached for a crayon and knocked over the clay pot. The librarian looked at the mess and asked John, "What happened here?"
"I knocked over the pot," said John quietly.
John kicked a little pebble along the path. It rolled and rolled and stopped by a patch of clover.
openings.rest:
John used a small shovel in the sandbox. John made a big sandcastle.
The librarian looked at Molly. "Never leave anyone out on purpose," the librarian said.
John and Molly walked to the edge of the water. Molly picked up many small shells.
John and Molly played a rolling game with a ball. The rule was one roll each. It was John's turn, and Molly looked away.
John could have rolled the ball twice, but John rolled it once and lost.
John looked over at the big oak tree. Its branches swayed gently back and forth, back and forth.
Molly tried to help pour the juice and tipped the cup over. The librarian looked at the mess and asked Molly, "What happened here?"
"I tipped the cup over," said Molly.
Molly noticed an ant carrying a crumb across the step. It went one way, then the other, and then it was gone.
Then John and Molly went home, tired and ready for bed.

openings.opening:
After breakfast, Bob and Amy went to play on the sidewalk. The coach came along.
Amy bumped into a small toy car. The car rolled into the street. The coach walked over and asked Amy, "Who did it?"
"It was not Bob," said Amy. "I bumped the car."
Amy sat down on the grass for a moment. A little breeze came by and made the leaves whisper.
The coach looked at Bob. "Never break other people's things," the coach said.
openings.rest:
Bob put Bob's bread down and went to ask the coach for a drink. Amy sat right next to the bread.
Amy picked up Bob's bread and handed it back. "Here is your bread," said Amy.
Then Amy stretched both arms up high and yawned. Somewhere nearby, a bell rang once and stopped.
Amy set Amy's toy truck down and bent to tie a shoe. Bob was right beside the truck.
Bob picked up Amy's toy truck and held it out. "You dropped this," said Bob.
Bob kicked a little pebble along the path. It rolled and rolled and stopped by a patch of clover.
Amy and Bob played a counting game with blocks. The rule was to count out loud, one at a time. It was Amy's turn, and Bob looked away.
Amy could have skipped a number, but Amy counted the blocks correctly and lost.
The sun came out from behind a cloud and warmed Amy's face. Amy blinked and looked around the yard.
Bob knocked over the box of blocks while playing next to Amy. The coach looked at the mess and asked Bob, "What happened here?"
"I knocked over the blocks," said Bob.
A moment later, Bob heard a dog barking somewhere far away. Then it was quiet again, and Bob went on.
Bob found a large blanket and a stick. Bob used the stick to hold the blanket up. Bob made a small fort on the sidewalk.
Soon the coach called Bob and Amy in for dinner.

openings.opening:
One day Billy and Joe were playing under the big tree. The teacher was nearby.
The teacher looked at Billy. "Do not break other people's things," the teacher said.
Joe sang a song while pushing the toy truck, and the tune went all wrong. Billy sat right next to Joe.
"That was a pretty song," said Billy.
Just then, a yellow leaf floated down and landed near Billy's shoe. Billy watched it wobble in the wind.
openings.rest:
Joe ran past Billy's sandcastle and knocked the top off it. The teacher looked at the mess and asked Joe, "What happened here?"
"I knocked it over," said Joe quietly. "I am sorry."
Joe sat down on the grass for a moment. A little breeze came by and made the leaves whisper.
The teacher pointed to a picture book on the grass. "Do not touch this book," the teacher said. Then the teacher walked away.
Billy looked at the book. Billy sat on the grass and played with a leaf instead.
Then Billy noticed a small brown bird on the fence. The bird hopped twice and flew away over the trees.
Joe found a small bike. Joe sat on the bike and rode it around.
Billy set Billy's glass of milk down and ran to look at a bird. Joe was right next to the milk.
Joe saw the milk. Joe did not touch the milk and stayed on the bike.
Joe looked over at the big oak tree. Its branches swayed gently back and forth, back and forth.
Billy tried to help with the drawing and spilled water all over it. The teacher looked at the mess and asked Billy, "What happened here?"
"I spilled the water," said Billy quietly. "I am sorry."
Then Billy stretched both arms up high and yawned. Somewhere nearby, a bell rang once and stopped.
The sun went down. Billy and Joe went inside for dinner.

openings.opening:
Jane and Sally were at the library on a warm afternoon. The teacher was nearby.
Sally put Sally's picture book down and went to get a drink. Jane sat right next to the book.
Jane picked up Sally's book and handed it to Sally. "Here is your book," said Jane.
After that, Jane looked up at the clouds for a while. The clouds drifted slowly across the big blue sky.
Sally jumped over the puzzle and scattered the pieces. The teacher looked at the mess and asked Sally, "What happened here?"
"I jumped over the puzzle," said Sally quietly. "I made the mess."
Then Sally noticed a small brown bird on the fence. The bird hopped twice and flew away over the trees.
openings.rest:
Jane found a packet of seeds and a small shovel in the library play area. Jane used the shovel to pretend to bake a cake with the seeds.
Sally and Jane played a tossing game with dice and a bucket. The rule was one throw each. It was Sally's turn, and Jane looked away.
Sally could have thrown the die twice, but Sally threw it only once.
A moment later, Sally heard a dog barking somewhere far away. Then it was quiet again, and Sally went on.
Jane and Sally played a stacking game with blocks. The rule was one block per turn. It was Jane's turn, and Sally looked away.
Jane could have added two blocks, but Jane only added one block.
Jane sat down on the grass for a moment. A little breeze came by and made the leaves whisper.
Sally saw a picture of a blue pool in a book. Sally pretended to swim through the pages.
The teacher looked at Jane. The teacher said, "Never say things that are not true."
Soon the teacher called Jane and Sally in for dinner.
